svg.text: Requirements — Uber (the hardest proximity-search problem)
board says: FRs are satisfied by the high-level design · NFRs choose your deep dives · CAP matters more than DAU here
Functional (3 — small on purpose)
FR1 · input start + destination → get a fare estimate
(ETA + price, one car type UberX)
FR2 · request a ride → matched to a nearby available
driver in real time (estimate → request → match)
FR3 · driver accepts / denies the request, then
navigates to pickup → dropoff
Out of scope (say it, then stop):
multiple car types · ratings · scheduled rides
Non-functional (quantified + in context)
NFR1 · low-latency MATCHING — target < 1 min to match
or fail, then tell the rider "no drivers available"
NFR2 · STRONG consistency OF MATCHING (CAP trade)
one ride → one driver, 1:1, never two of each
NFR3 · high availability EVERYTHING OUTSIDE matching
serve 24/7, minimize downtime, stay reliable
NFR4 · high throughput in SURGES — stadiums / NYE /
Taylor Swift out: ~hundreds of thousands of
requests within one region
Back-of-envelope rule (from the video, say it):
skip estimate math up front — only compute when a number can change the design.
Example: 3M active drivers × heartbeats every 5s ≈ 600k writes/s — THAT number picks the DB (deep dive 1).
Where the CAP choice lands (this is the Uber twist):
consistency FOR MATCHING (never double-book a driver) + availability for every other path —
same "stale reads, exact writes" asymmetry you already know from Ticketmaster.
